name: Arcane Ace
body:
Some dealers can use legerdemain in their card skills, others actually infuse their card skill with arcane energies.

Class Skills: An arcane ace gains Knowledge (arcana) and Spellcraft instead of Acrobatics and Stealth.

Spot the Components: An arcane ace gains a bonus equal to their dealer class level on Spellcraft checks to identify spells as they are being cast.

Cantrips: Arcane aces can know a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, each day, as noted on Table: Arcane Ace Spells Known. These spells are cast normally, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again.

Spells: An arcane ace casts arcane spells drawn from the sorcerer/wizard spell list. An arcane ace casts any spell they know without preparing it ahead of time. To learn or cast a spell, an arcane ace must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against An arcane ace’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the arcane ace’s Charisma modifier.

Like other spellcasters, an arcane ace can cast only a certain number of spells of each level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Arcane Ace Spells per Day. In addition, he receives bonus spells per day if they have a high Charisma score (see Table 1–3: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells in the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook). The arcane ace does not need to prepare these spells in advance; they can cast any spell they know at any time, assuming they haven’t yet used up their allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level.

The arcane ace’s selection of spells is limited. An arcane ace gains more spells as they increase in level, as indicated on Table: Arcane Ace Spells Known. Unlike spells per day, the number of spells an arcane ace knows is not affected by their Charisma score. At 8th level and every three levels thereafter, an arcane ace can choose to learn a new spell in place of one they already know. In effect, the arcane ace loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged. An arcane ace may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that they gain new spells known for the level. Their caster level is equal to their arcane ace level – 3 (minimum 1). This ability replaces charmed life and bonus feats.

Charge Card (Su)

At 1st level, an arcane ace can infuse a thrown card with arcane energy. They can expend 1 Gambit point as a swift action to grant their deck of combat cards a +1 enhancement bonus for 1 minute. Every four levels beyond 1st, the deck gains another +1 enhancement bonus, to a maximum of +5 at 17th level. These bonuses can be added to the combat card deck, stacking with existing weapon enhancement to a maximum of +5.

Multiple uses of this ability do not stack with themselves.

At 5th level, these bonuses can be used to add any weapon properties to the deck. Adding these properties consumes an amount of bonus equal to the property’s base price modifier (see the Magic Weapon Special Ability Descriptions). These properties are added to any the deck already has, but duplicates do not stack.

If the combat card deck is not magical, at least a +1 enhancement bonus must be added before any other properties can be added.

These bonuses and properties are decided when the Gambit point is spent and cannot be changed until the next time the arcane ace uses this ability. These bonuses do not function if the combat card deck is wielded by anyone other than the Arcane ace. An arcane ace can only enhance one combat card deck in this way at one time. If they use this ability again, the first use immediately ends.

This ability replaces the following tricks: bad beat, killer hand, card trick, cutting edge, perfect flip and final card.

School of Cards

At 1st level, the arcane ace chooses a school of magic (similar to a wizard).

They gain a bonus spell per day for each spell level usable only with spells of that spell school. The cost of such specialization is that they must select two opposition schools. Any spells from those two opposition schools cost 2 spell slots to cast. If the arcane ace selects universal as their spell school, they do not gain bonus spells and nor do they have to select opposition schools.

Any DCs for the abilities listed below are equal to (DC 10 + 1/2 the arcane ace’s class levels + their Charisma modifier) unless otherwise stated.

Additionally, their choice of spell school changes what tricks they can perform with their cards. An arcane ace replaces the following tricks with the tricks below depending upon their chosen spell school: good hand, speed deal, quick deal, dirty flip, master gambler, and dazing display. If the arcane ace chose universalist, they do not lose the previously mentioned tricks but they do not gain new tricks from below.

Abjuration
Guarded Card (Su)

At 1st level, an abjuration-focused arcane ace can, as an immediate action, spend a Gambit point and a use of attack of opportunity to throw up a magical barrier from a tossed card. Doing so grants the arcane ace a deflection bonus to their AC equal to their Charisma bonus against the triggering attack. The tossed card blocks the attack with its magic force.

Covered Hand (Su)

At 3rd level, an abjuration-focused arcane ace is constantly shielded by some minor arcane energies. As long as they have at least 1 Gambit point remaining they have a resistance bonus to 1 saving throw equal to 1/4 their arcane ace class levels (minimum +1). The save receiving the bonus may be chosen or changed as a move action. counterspell as the spell dispel magic using your arcane ace class level as the caster level for the effect.

Trump Card (Su)

At 7th level, an abjuration-focused arcane ace can thwart other spellcasters. They may spend a point of Gambit to throw a specially charged card as one of their attacks. Given the nature of the card, it cannot benefit from the charge card ability. If the attack with the trump card succeeds you may do a targeted dispel or counterspell as the spell dispel magic using your arcane ace class level as the caster level for the effect.

Calling the Bluff (Su)

At 11th level, an abjuration-focused arcane ace can thwart the attempts by others to enchant or trick them. If they have at least 1 point of Gambit remaining and succeed on a saving throw against an enchantment or illusion effect, the arcane ace may identify the effect as if they had succeeded on a Spellcraft check to do so. Additionally, the arcane ace gains a +20 bonus to Bluff checks to pretend they are affected by the spell.

Discard (Su)

At 15th level, an abjuration-focused arcane ace can spend a point of Gambit to instill a card thrown in one of their normal attacks with banishing power. If the card hits, it deals damage as normal, however, if the creature is a summoned creature or is extraplanar, they must make a Will save or be banished back to their home plane.

Magic Foil (Su)

At 19th level, an abjuration-focused arcane ace can, as an immediate action, toss up a card, spend a Gambit point and a use of attack of opportunity to negate a spell of up to 5th level cast upon them or a spell that includes the arcane ace in the area. The thrown card interposes itself between the arcane ace and the spell and thwarts it. This includes spells, spell-like abilities and spell effects created by items. For the purposes of determining the level of the spell, refer to the lesser globe of invulnerability spell.

Conjuration
Card Blind (Su)

At 1st level, a conjuration-focused arcane ace can throw a magically charged card at a spot within 10 feet as a standard action and by expending a point of Gambit. The arcane ace must succeed at a ranged attack roll similar to a thrown weapon (vs. AC 5). If the attack roll succeeds, the arcane ace creates a 5-foot tall card on one edge of the target square. The card provides full cover as if it were a full wall. The card has a hardness of 4 and hit points equal to 2 + your Charisma modifier. The card remains in place for 1 round per arcane ace level or until destroyed. At 3th level and every 3 levels thereafter, the dealer can throw an additional card in the same action to add another 5-foot section of wall adjacent to one of the other cards thrown in this action. The edges of such additional cards must be touching the edge of one of the other cards thrown in the same action.

Shuffled (Su)

At 3rd level, a conjuration-focused arcane ace never loses their cards. As long as they have at least 1 Gambit point remaining, any thrown cards may be instantly returned to the deck and shuffled in at a random point. In addition, they may spend a point of Gambit to teleport their deck of cards into their hands as a free action.

Anchoring Card (Su)

At 7th level, a conjuration-focused arcane ace can instill a card with an anchoring magic force. They may spend a point of Gambit to instill a card thrown during a normal attack action with this power. If the card hits, it lodges into them and causes all movement by the creature to cost double the normal amount. This effect also affects incorporeal creatures. In addition to the movement penalty and normal damage, the card prevents extraplanar travel by the target. The effect lasts 1 round per arcane ace level or until the target spends a full-round action to dislodge the card, however doing so provokes an attack of opportunity and deals the base damage of the combat card. E.G. no Dex or precision damage, but the normal dice damage and any enhancements or charge card damage. Once the duration of the effect ends, the card dislodges of its own accord dealing no additional damage.

Card Toss (Su)

At 11th level, as long as the conjuration-based arcane ace has at least 1 point of Gambit remaining, they teleport to a card they toss as a standard action. To do so, the arcane ace must succeed against a ranged attack on the space they wish to occupy similar to a thrown weapon (vs. AC 5). Once the card lands, the arcane ace can teleport to where the card landed. The arcane ace may expend a point of Gambit to bring any willing creatures they are touching when the card lands with them. The teleported creatures including the arcane ace retain their original positioning in the new place. If this would place them in a hazard, they may make a DC 15 Reflex save to move to a safe adjacent space if applicable.

Go Fish (Su)

At 15th level, a conjuration-focused arcane ace can throw a specially charged card by expending a point of Gambit as part of their normal attacks. If the thrown card hits the target, in addition to normal damage, the target must make a Will save. If the hit target fails their saving throw, the arcane ace and the target switch places via teleportation.

House of Cards (Sp)

At 19th level, a conjuration-focused arcane ace can spend 1 point of Gambit to create a house of cards with their whole deck of combat cards. Creating the house of cards takes ten minutes of work which need not be consecutive. Once completed, the house of cards leads to an extradimensional space. Only the arcane ace and creatures they designate may enter the house of cards by touching the card structure. The arcane ace may set a passphrase to allow entry if they so wish. The inside of the extradimensional space is a 20 foot cube appointed with furniture of the arcane ace’s choosing. The space is atmosphere controlled however the structure and the furniture within all seem to be made from the cards used by the arcane ace. The house of cards lasts for 24 hours or until disassembled. If creatures remain inside when the effect ends or the house of cards is disassembled/knocked over, they are shunted back out of the house. When the effect ends normally, the house of cards collapses back into a perfectly shuffled deck.

Divination
Counting Cards (Sp)

At 1st level, a divination-focused arcane ace can spend 1 point of Gambit as a standard action to instill divination magic into a card. When activating this ability, the arcane ace must select between magic, alignment, creature type, or secrets. The card must be held in one hand to use this ability but it does not require concentration. If the card is dropped or returned to its deck, this ability ends. Otherwise, this ability remains active for 1 minute per dealer level. Regardless of what it is detecting, the card will change color based on what the dealer has chosen to detect and will grow brighter with proximity to what you are detecting. What colors correspond to what is unique to the arcane ace. The card cannot tell the arcane ace the power or number of detectable objects in the room, simply the closest qualifying target and its proximity to the arcane ace. The detection is within a 60-foot cone originating from the back of the card.

If the arcane ace selects magic, the card detects the closest aura of magic, changes color to designate the school of magic and its intensity based on proximity to the closest magic aura.

If the arcane ace selects alignment, the card changes color to reflect the alignment of the closest person within the detection cone.

If the arcane ace selects creature type, the arcane ace selects a particular creature type to detect and if it appears within the detection cone, the card changes color and glows based on the creature’s proximity.

If the arcane ace selects secrets, the card will detect secret doors, treasure, and traps. The closest one of each will be detected by the card.

Peeking at the Hand (Sp)

At 3rd level, a divination-focused arcane ace can turn a drawn card into a magical lens only they can see through. As long as the arcane ace has at least 1 Gambit remaining, they can draw a card as a standard action and hold the card up to their eye, they can see invisible or ethereal creatures as if under the effect of see invisibility. The arcane ace can only see the invisible or ethereal creatures by looking through the cone, so treat it as a cone originating from the arcane ace. Additionally, the arcane ace can spend a point of Gambit to add the additional ability to see all the creatures’ surface thoughts printed in little speech bubbles around them. The creature may make a Will save to resist their surface thoughts being shown in this way. If the creature makes their Will save, they are immune to this ability for 24 hours. No one else but the arcane ace can use the power of this card and if the card is dropped or returned to the deck, the effect ends. Otherwise it lasts for a number of rounds equal to the arcane ace’s class level.

Harrowing (Sp)

At 7th level, a divination-focused arcane ace can use their combat cards as a harrow deck. Additionally, they may spend 1 point of Gambit to cast the spell harrowing. At 15th level, the arcane ace can instead use the point of Gambit to cast greater harrowing.

Call (Su)

At 11th level, as long as the divination-focused arcane ace has at least 1 point of Gambit, they can draw a combat card and toss it into a particular square similar to a thrown weapon (vs. AC 5). When the card lands it glows with magical energy and reveals the presence of illusions within 60 feet. All creatures, objects or locations under the effect of an illusion spell, magic items with an illusion aura, and shapechangers are limned with a glow similar to the spell faerie fire. This does not show the true nature of the limned target, but it would reveal invisible creatures. The card continues to exude the aura for 1 minute per arcane ace class level or until the card is picked up or moved from its location.

Mind Link (Su)

At 15th level, a divination-focused arcane ace can draw combat cards and instill them with a mental connection. By spending 1 point of Gambit, they may draw a number of cards equal to 1/3 their arcane ace class level (rounded down). Each drawn card can be given to a creature and for as long as they keep the card in their possession, they are able to telepathically communicate with you and any other card-holder. This mind link lasts for 10 minutes per arcane ace class level even if the card changes hands or is dropped.

Seeing the Long Game (Su)

At 19th level, the divination-focused arcane ace has turned their combat cards into a conduit of divination magic. Their combat cards may be used as a focus for scrying and by spending 1 point of Gambit, they may use the spell greater scrying. The arcane ace may use counting cards or peeking at the hand through this scrying connection without spending additional Gambit so long as they have at least 1 Gambit remaining.

Enchantment
Startling Card (Su)

At 1st level, an enchantment-focused arcane ace can spend a point of Gambit to charge one of the cards thrown during their normal attack action with energy. If the card hits it affects the creature’s mind with startling power. The target must make a Will save or suffer a penalty equal to twice the arcane ace’s class level to the next attack roll or skill check made by the target in the next minute. This is a mind-affecting, compulsion effect.

Table Talk (Su)

At 3rd level, an enchantment-focused arcane ace can, as long as they have 1 point of Gambit remaining, shuffle their combat cards or play a card game to make their speech preternaturally put people at ease. While shuffling their combat cards or playing a card game with a creature, the arcane ace gets a bonus to this Diplomacy check equal to their arcane ace class level. Additionally, a successful check moves the target’s disposition 2 levels. This ability may be used in combat to make a hostile creature non-hostile. At 8th level, this ability may be used on any creature regardless of shared language. However, if there is no shared language, the arcane ace suffers a -5 penalty to the Diplomacy check. This is a mind-affecting, emotion effect.

Stunning Card (Su)

At 7th level, an enchantment-focused can, as a standard action, throw a specially charged card at a target. If the card hits, in addition to normal damage, the target must make a Will save or have their mind overloaded with information stunning them for 1 round per arcane ace class level. The creature is allowed a new save at the beginning of their turn after the first round of the effect. If the creature succeeds on the initial save or the subsequent rounds’ save, they are stead staggered for the round. This is a mind-affecting, compulsion effect.

Overwhelming Skill (Su)

At 11th level, as long as the enchantment-focused arcane ace has at least 1 point of Gambit remaining, creatures they target with enchantment or mind-affecting spells or effects no longer benefit from their protections. The creature does not gain any benefit from saving throw bonuses against enchantment or mind-affecting effects. If the target is immune to such effects, they are instead treated as having a +4 bonus to their saving throw. Additionally, if the target has spell resistance, the arcane ace can spend 1 point of Gambit to bypass the spell resistance. The effect must be an arcane ace spell or class ability.

Befuddling Card (Su)

At 15th level, the enchantment-focused arcane ace can throw a special card that clouds the mind of the target. As a part of one of their normal attacks, they can spend 1 point of Gambit to add the extra effect. If the card hits, the target must make a Will save. If they fail, they are affected as per the confusion spell and they suffer a -10 penalty on Wisdom checks and Will saves. They may make a Will save each round at the end of their turn, albeit at the penalized Will save, to end the effect early. Otherwise, this effect lasts for 1 round per arcane ace class level. This is a mind-affecting effect.

Your Lucky Card (Sp)

At 19th level, the enchantment-focused arcane ace can charge a set of cards to grant a sense of bravery and heroism to the holders. As a standard action you can draw five cards and spend 1 point of Gambit to charge the cards with energy. Each card grants the bearer a +2 morale bonus to all checks, attack rolls, saves, and weapon damage rolls. A single target can carry up to 2 cards at a time and the bonuses stack. The cards lose their charge after 10 minutes. This is a mind-affecting, emotion effect.

Evocation
Guided Toss (Su)

At 1st level, an evocation-focused arcane ace can spend a point of Gambit as a swift action to change one of the cards thrown during an attack sequence into an unerring card of force. The card thrown in this manner loses any benefit normally granted due to skill with the combat card, like Weapon Specialization or dealer’s cut, nor do they add their Strength or Dexterity to damage. The force-card strikes unerringly and does not require an attack roll. The damage dealt by this card is force damage and is subject to deflection or negation by spells or items that protect against magic missiles.

Face Up, Face Down (Sp)

At 3rd level, an evocation-based arcane ace can instill energy into a drawn card as a standard action to make it glow brightly or draw light from the surrounding area. As long as the arcane ace has at least 1 point of Gambit remaining, they may draw a card and choose to either make it glow as per the light spell or reduce the light level by 1 step as per the darkness spell. The card can then be handed off or thrown if so wished. At 7th level, the arcane ace can spend an additional standard action to instill additional energy into the card, increasing its effect to be considered daylight or lowering the light level by two steps and preventing darkvision from penetrating the radius. This charge lasts for 1 hour and the arcane ace may only have one such card active at a time. This card does not counter or dispel other light or darkness spells however, it can suppress such spells of lower effective spell level than it or be suppressed by spells of higher spell level than it in any overlapping area. For this purpose the effective spell level of the card is half the arcane ace’s class level (minimum 1).

Explosive Reveal (Sp)

At 7th level, as a standard action, an evocation-focused arcane ace can throw an elementally charged card that explodes in a 20-foot radius by expending 1 point of Gambit. The explosion deals 1d6 points of damage per 2 arcane ace class level plus their Charisma modifier, of an elemental chosen from acid, cold, electricity, fire or sonic at the time the card is thrown. All creatures within the blast radius are allowed a Reflex save to halve the damage. The card is not harmed by the explosion and remains on the ground at the center of the explosion.

Elemental Card (Su)

At 11th level, as long as an evocation-focused arcane ace has at least 1 point of Gambit remaining, they may, as a swift action, change the damage type of one card thrown or card melee attack made during the round to deal elemental damage instead of the normal piercing or slashing damage. The elemental damage type is chosen from acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic when the attack is made. A sonic card does not function in an area of silence. The attack loses Dexterity to damage and instead adds their Charisma modifier to the damage. All other enhancements to the damage are added normally.

Covering Your Hand (Su)

At 15th level, an evocation-focused arcane ace can spend a full-round action to charge up to 10 drawn cards by spending a point of Gambit. For 1 hour after the cards are charged, one may be thrown as part of an attack action or up to 3 cards as a standard action. This card will not hit a target, instead it stops and hovers in a square and creates a 5-foot section of a wall made of force as per the wall of force spell. Once the card is deployed in this way, the wall of force remains active for one round per arcane ace class level or until the arcane ace dismisses it as a swift action. If a section of the wall is subject to a disintegrate spell, the wall dissipates as normal but the card is unharmed, unless separately hit by such an effect.

Put some Spin on It (Su)

At 19th level, an evocation-focused arcane ace can throw a card charged with a magical spin that creates a spinning blade of force extending from the card. Doing so costs 1 point of Gambit. The spinning blade of force can be directed to attack any targets within 60 feet of the arcane ace. If the arcane ace moves more than 60 feet from the spinning blade, it must return within that range at the next available opportunity. The blade can move 60 feet per round and make a single attack against a target at the arcane ace’s direction. The blade uses the arcane ace’s base attack bonus + their Charisma bonus +3 to determine its attack bonus. If the attack hits, it deals 2d4 + the arcane ace’s Charisma modifier + 3 force damage and it has a 19-20/x2 critical. The blade cannot provide or benefit from flanking. This spinning force-blade lasts for 1 round per arcane ace class level or until dismissed.

Illusion
Colored Suits (Su)

At 1st level, an illusion-focused arcane ace can spend 1 point of Gambit as a standard action to cause one of their cards to explode into a spray of smaller, colorful cards. This is only an illusion and the thrown card is not damaged in any way. All creatures within a 15-foot cone must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the arcane ace’s class levels plus their Charisma modifier). On a failure the creatures are blinded and stunned for 1d4 rounds, then dazzled for a number of rounds equal to the arcane ace’s class level. If the creature succeeds, they are only dazzled for 1d4 rounds. This ability does not affect sightless creatures.

Mesmerizing Shuffle (Su)

At 3rd level, an illusion-based arcane ace can perform a set of shuffling maneuvers so intricate it fascinates any observers. As long as the arcane ace has a Gambit point remaining, they can use a standard action each round to perform this magical shuffle. The arcane ace can affect a number of HD worth of creatures equal to their 1/2 their class level plus their Charisma modifier who can see the performance. Those with the fewest HD are affected first. Those affected must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the arcane ace’s class levels plus their Charisma modifier) or be fascinated for as long as the arcane ace keeps up the performance.

Face Card (Su)

At 7th level, as a full-round action and expending a point of Gambit, the arcane ace can instill illusion magic and a minor bit of their consciousness into a card. The card must then be thrown into a square (a ranged attack roll similar to a thrown weapon (vs. AC 5) If the attack is successful, it creates a major image spell effect that does not require concentration. The image will move and perform its actions as if concentrated on due to the instilled consciousness. The DC to disbelieve this illusion is 10 + 1/2 the arcane ace’s class levels + their Charisma modifier. The illusion lasts for a number of rounds equal to the arcane ace’s Charisma modifier.

Now You See Me, Now You Don’t (Su)

At 11th level, an illusion-focused arcane ace can draw and charge a card as a standard action and turn themself invisible as per the spell invisibility. This ability remains in effect as long as the conditions of the underlying spell are met, the arcane ace maintains at least 1 point of Gambit, they maintain concentration on the effect and hold the card in one hand over their face. This effect lasts up to 1 hour maximum per day.

Poker Face (Su)

At 15th level, an illusion-focused arcane ace may draw up to 1 specially-charged card per 5 class levels as a standard action using one Gambit. The card allows the target to change their shape as per the disguise self spell. The form taken is at the discretion of the card holder and may be changed by concentrating on the card as a standard action. The possessor is only affected by the card if it is held or on their person, tucked in their belt, in a pocket, etc. If the card is dropped it loses its charge. Otherwise, the effect lasts for a number of minutes equal to the arcane ace’s class level.

Doubling (Sp)

At 19th level, an illusion-focused arcane ace can, as a standard action. expend a point of Gambit to throw down a card either in an adjacent square or as a ranged attack into a square like a thrown weapon (vs. AC 5). When it lands, it creates a quasi-real shadow version of the arcane ace. It has all the equipment and stats of the arcane ace but is unable to use Gambit or cast spells and has 1/2 the arcane ace’s total hit points. If the arcane ace is benefiting from a beneficial spell or has charge card active, the shadow duplicate also benefits. The shadow duplicate attacks with the arcane ace’s attack bonuses, ability bonuses and damage, though they only deal 60% of normal damage. A creature attacking or attacked by the shadow duplicate may make a Will save to disbelieve. If they succeed, the shadow duplicate deals no damage to them though they may still be damaged by them. The shadow duplicate acts on its own and does not require direction or concentration from the arcane ace. It may provide flanking and benefit from flanking from any creature that has not succeeded on a Will save against it. The shadow duplicate lasts for a number of rounds equal to the arcane ace’s class level or until it is reduced to 0 or fewer hit points.

Necromancy
Dark Card (Su)

At 1st level, a necromancy-focused arcane ace can throw a card charged with vile necromantic energy as one of their attacks during a round by expending a point of Gambit. If the card hits, it deals an additional 1d6 negative energy damage. Additionally, the target must make a Fortitude save or be sickened for a number of rounds equal to the negative energy damage. If the target is normally healed by negative energy damage, they are healed by 1d6 but must make a Will save or be panicked for a number of rounds equal to the healing. This panicked condition affects all undead regardless of immunity to fear or mindaffecting due to an ability or being mindless.

Deal on the Low Road (Su)

At 3rd level, so long as the necromancy-focused arcane ace maintains 1 point of Gambit, they may draw a card and hold it in one hand to attempt to command an undead creature. Drawing the card is a standard action and the card must remain in the arcane ace’s hand while the effect is active. The undead creature must make a Will save or be under the influence of the arcane ace as per the command undead spell.

Leeching Card (Su)

At 7th level, a necromancy-focused arcane ace can spend a point of Gambit to throw a specially charged card as one of their attacks during the round. If the card hits, it draws the life essence from the target and heals the arcane ace for the damage dealt, any healing that would exceed the arcane ace’s maximum hit points instead becomes temporary hit points that last for 1 hour. This card can draw life energy from any living or undead creature but it has no extra effect on constructs or objects.

Animating Deal (Sp)

At 11th level, a necromancy-focused arcane ace can draw a card as a standard action and place it upon the forehead of a corpse animating it as per the spell animate dead. As long as the arcane ace maintains 1 point of Gambit, the undead remains animated and under the control of the arcane ace. The arcane ace can maintain only a single undead in this manner and if the undead is destroyed, or if the arcane ace dies or has no Gambit remaining or the arcane ace ends the effect, the card drops and the undead disintegrates, unable to be animated again.

Terrifying Flip (Su)

At 15th level, a necromancy-based arcane ace can throw a card charged with dark and terrifying power as one of their normal attacks during the round by expending a point of Gambit. If the card hits, in addition to normal damage, the target must make a Will save or be panicked for 1d8 rounds then shaken for 1 hour. If the target makes their saving throw, they are only shaken for 1 hour. If the target is immune to fear or mind-affecting effects, they instead are staggered for 1d8 rounds with no saving throw.

Dead Man’s Hand (Su)

At 19th level, a necromancy-based arcane ace can throw a card filled with deadly energy as one of their attacks in a round by spending a point of Gambit. If the card hits, in addition to normal damage, the card deals 10 negative energy damage per arcane ace class level. The target is allowed a Fortitude saving throw to save themself. If they succeed, the card only deals an extra 3d8 + their arcane ace class levels in negative energy damage. This is considered a death effect.

Transmutation
Oversized Cards (Su)

At 1st level, a transmutation-focused arcane ace can instill magic into their combat cards that cause them to grow in size when thrown by spending a point of Gambit as a swift action. This affects a number of cards equal to the arcane ace’s class level. If one of the magically-charged cards is thrown, it grows in size and deals one die category larger of damage than normal (1d6 for Medium, 1d4 for Small). At 8th level, this increases an additional die (1d8 for Medium, 1d6 for Small) and an additional die at 16th level (2d6 for Medium, 1d8 for Small). The card reverts to normal size after it hits (or misses). If the cards are not used within 10 minutes, they lose their charge.

Extraordinary Hand (Su)

At 3rd level, so long as the transmutation-focused arcane ace maintains at least 1 point of Gambit they gain an enhancement bonus to Strength, Constitution or Dexterity. The attribute may be changed by taking a full-round action to shift the stored power. The enhancement bonus is equal to 1/4 the arcane ace’s class level +1.

Empowering Card (Su)

At 7th level, a transmutation-focused arcane ace can instill energy into a combat card and affix it to a weapon, shield or set of armor. Doing so is a standard action and uses 1 point of Gambit. The card remains affixed to the weapon for 1 hour per arcane ace class level and grants the weapon an increase in enhancement bonus of +1 per 4 class levels the arcane ace possesses. The enhancement can instead provide a special ability to the item. This card cannot make the item go above the normal enchantment limits (+5 max enhancement and +10 total bonus). The effect ends early if the card is removed from the item, once affixed, the card is not transferable to another item.

Reshuffle Identity (Su)

At 11th level, a transmutation-focused arcane ace can draw a magically-charged card and tuck it into a pocket as a standard action costing 1 point of Gambit. So long as the card is not dropped or returned to its deck and the arcane ace maintains at least 1 gambit, they can change their appearance as per the alter self spell as a swift action.

Open Hand (Su)

At 15th level, a transmutation-focused arcane ace can draw a card as a standard action and affix it to a solid surface or container. Doing so costs 1 point of Gambit. The arcane ace can then pull at the corners of the card to make it as large as a 20-foot tall door. The arcane ace can then ‘open’ the card to reveal a new hatch into a container, or a door leading into a hallway through the solid surface. The opening beyond the card-door extends until the next open space or 5 feet per 2 arcane ace levels, whichever is shorter. If the passage beyond the card-door reaches its maximum depth without reaching an open space, it is just an alcove. The card-door remains affixed for 1 hour per arcane ace class level or until the arcane ace removes it. If creatures are within the passage created by the effect then the card is removed or the duration expires, they are shunted harmlessly into the closest open space.

Double Play (Su)

At 19th level, a transmutation-focused arcane ace can throw a specially charged card as one of their attacks during the round by spending a point of Gambit. If the card hits the target, in addition to the normal damage dealt by the card, the arcane ace can propel the creature to strike another target or surface within 30 feet with their body. The arcane ace rolls an additional attack roll using the same attack bonus used for the initial attack. If the second attack hits the target creature and the secondary target, if applicable, take 1d4 per size category, starting with Diminutive, plus the arcane ace’s Charisma bonus. A critical hit on this second attack counts as a combat card critical for the purposes of regaining Gambit. If the attack misses, treat the attack as a thrown weapon miss and the original target still takes the damage. Once the original target strikes a surface or another creature, the card dislodges and returns to the arcane ace.

Magic Hand (Su)

At 20th level, the arcane ace’s magic hands constantly infuse their cards. They may use charge card as a free action and it no longer costs a Gambit point to activate.

Luckmaker Most dealers have luck and skill that help them in their craft, luckmakers make their own luck to stack the deck in their favor. Lucky Draws A lucky draw operates similarly to a Gambit, but it reflects the luckmakers ability to shift and change fate using their deck of combat cards. Unless otherwise noted, a lucky draw does not provoke an attack of opportunity. The save DC against a lucky draw (if applicable) is equal to 10 + 1/2 the luckmaker’s class levels + the luckmaker’s Charisma modifier. Got Your Number (Su) The luckmaker can spend a point of Gambit to draw a card that causes a target within 30 feet to have bad luck. This is a standard action that does not require the card to be thrown. The target takes a -2 penalty to one of the following (luckmaker’s choice): AC, ability checks, attack rolls, saving throws, or skill checks. This change in luck lasts for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the luckmaker’s Charisma modifier. A Will save reduces this duration to just 1 round. This is a curse effect. At 11th level the penalty becomes -4. At 15th level, a luckmaker can activate this ability to affect all opponents within 30 feet. This ability replaces the bad beat, cutting edge, and across the table tricks. Fold (Su) At 7th level, the luckmaker can draw a card that causes the target to accidentally fumble. This is a standard action that expends 1 point of Gambit and does not require the card to be thrown. This shift in fortune forces the target, a single opponent within 30 feet, to fumble. They drop one held item or fall prone (as selected by the luckmaker). A successful Will save instead staggers the opponent for 1 round. This is a curse effect. This ability replaces the quick deal trick. Cursed Card (Su) At 19th level, when the luckmaker hits a target with a special card, they can immediately spend a point of Gambit to cause a dire curse to be placed on the target. The card itself leaves an obvious cursed mark on the target. This inflicts the target with the major curse spell effect if the target fails their Will save. If the major curse is dispelled, the mark left by the card is also removed. This ability replaces the final card Gambit. Lucky Dodge (Ex) Starting at 2nd level, a luckmaker gains a +1 luck bonus to AC while wearing light or no armor. Anything that causes the luckmaker to lose his Dexterity bonus to AC also causes him to lose this luck bonus. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd level (to a maximum of +5 at 20th level). This ability replaces nimble. Ace in the Hole (Su) Starting at 2nd level, a luckmaker can draw some cards at the beginning of the day, determining the course of the rest of the day. They may draw one card and tuck it away. They roll a d20 and hold onto the result. As an immediate action, they may draw the tucked away card and force the target to use the result of the held d20 roll. If used on an unwilling target, they are allowed a Will saving throw DC 10 + 1/2 the luckmaker’s class levels + the luckmaker’s Charisma modifier. The held card must be used when the target declares an action but before the roll is made. At 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the luck maker may draw an additional card to tuck away (to a maximum of 5 cards at 18th level). The luckmaker may expend a point of Gambit to replace a drawn or used card. This use of Gambit does not let them hold onto more cards than they would normally be able to. This ability replaces charmed life. Make my Own Luck (Ex) At 20th level, the luckmaker masters the ability to shift probabilities in their environment. The dealer gains an additional card to use with ace in the hole and may expend Gambit to go above their normal maximum. They no longer need to expend a point of Gambit to use got your number. Instead they need only maintain at least 1 point of Gambit to use it. This ability replaces master card. Combat Cards Cost 40 gp; Weight 1 lb.; Damage 1d3 (small), 1d4 (medium); Critical x2; Type piercing Range Increment 20 ft. (projectile); Category ranged; Proficiency exotic; Weapon Group thrown A deck of combat cards holds 52 playing cards of steel, bone or wood. These cards are special in that they are sharpened for dealing damage, though still good for a playing card game. These cards cannot be used as melee weapons. Although they are thrown weapons, combat cards are crafted as a set of 52 cards instead of individual cards. The cards are recoverable as normal thrown weapons.
